item.description: model: Add MiniCPM-OCR-Jev (#30980) * model : add MiniCPM-OCR-Jev support The model is a Qwen3.5-VL trunk with a value head read at the last token: it scores an OCR text against an image rendered from it, it does not generate. Add the openbmb-minicpm-ocr-jev decision type, served by POST /v1/systemone. The class scores are the pooled output of the sequence, read with last pooling, so the conversion turns score.weight into cls.output and sets embedding_length_out. The checkpoint has no LM head, so text generation is rejected instead of using the output weights duplicated from the token embeddings. The task is fixed, so its prompt is entirely in the systemone template, the same way h2o-lightning keeps its default there. The processor of the checkpoint allows up to 16384 merged tokens per image, more than the Qwen-VL default of mtmd, so the mmproj keeps the image budget of the preprocessor config. The checkpoint declares MiniCPMOCRForSequenceClassification in its config.json, as other models do. item.description: tests : fix multi-seq split replay and partial-state cases for trained models (#31216) * tests : fix multi-seq split replay against trained models The rollback snapshot is captured by the graph that decoded the rolled-back tail, while the reference context decodes the same prefix with different batch shapes. The two states differ in the last bits and trained models amplify the difference with every replayed token. Compare only the first replayed token of each seq, then restore the rollback state into the reference context before the seq-1-only tail. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : require bit-exact seq-1 isolation in split replay The seq state save is not always bit-lossless - SWA-masked cells are not saved - so reload the restored state back into the rollback context. That way both contexts enter the seq-1-only tail with byte-identical memory, including the cell layout, and the tail logits must match bit-exact. Also assert that the restored state round-trips bit-identical. Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (MacBook, M5 Max, 128GB) * tests : drop the n_swa partial-state check from ps The check keys off llama_model_n_swa(), which returns 0 for dsv4 even though its raw KV cache has a 128-cell sliding window. The partial state grows with the tokens there by design, so the flatness check is wrong. Keep the partial <= full invariant. item.description: ggml-cpu : rewrite concat as one row kernel for all types (#31179) Every dst row comes from src0 or src1, or for dim 0 from the row of src0 followed by the row of src1, so a single kernel covers every type: a dense source row is one memcpy, quantized types included, and a strided source is copied element by element with the element size known at compile time. Rows are split across threads instead of i2 alone, which is often 1, and are copied in tiles of 32: for a transposed source the elements are walked in the outer loop, so the rows of a tile read neighboring addresses instead of jumping a full row stride per element. The imatrix holds one vector of ne[0] values per 2D slice, so the expected size is ne[0]*ne[2]*ne[3], not ne[0]*ne[2]. This matches how the imatrix is indexed per row for 4D tensors in llama_tensor_quantize_impl. item.description: hip: fix bf16 WMMA operand vector type for gfx11/gfx12 (#30885) The __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_f32_16x16x16_bf16_w32 (and _gfx12) builtins take their A/B operands as vectors of short (_ExtVector<16, short> / _ExtVector<8, short>), not __bf16. The operand type has been short since the builtin was introduced, so this works across LLVM/ROCm versions without a version gate. Fixes HIP builds for RDNA3 (gfx1150/1151) and RDNA4 (gfx1200/1201).
